howItWorks.title: How does the calculator work?
howItWorks.step1: In the first part of the calculator, you fill in all the costs, together with the correct VAT category of your product.
howItWorks.step2: Then in the second part of the calculator you do the same, but with the revenue.
howItWorks.step3: Next, the totals will be added up and the Break Even ROAS will automatically appear in the bottom section.
howItWorks.step4: If you want to do a new calculation, click on the "Reset" button and you can enter new data.
howItWorks.step1_product: In the first part of the calculator, you fill in all the costs, together with the correct VAT category of your product.
howItWorks.step1_service: In the first part of the calculator, you fill in all the costs, together with the correct VAT category for your service or engagement.

whatIsBreakEven.title: What is the Break Even ROAS?
whatIsBreakEven.description1: With a Break Even ROAS you know exactly what ROAS you need for your ads to break even.
whatIsBreakEven.description2: So if your Break Even ROAS is 1.8 for example:
whatIsBreakEven.profitable: Every campaign, ad set/ad group or ad that has a ROAS higher than 1.8 is profitable.
whatIsBreakEven.losing: Every campaign, ad set/ad group or ad that has a ROAS lower than 1.8 is losing you money.
whatIsBreakEven.breakEven: And of course on every campaign, ad set/ad group or ad that has a ROAS of 1.8 you are break even.

whyImportant.title: Why is it so important?
whyImportant.description1: Calculating the Break Even ROAS is very important.
whyImportant.description2: Facebook, TikTok and Snapchat for example indicates for every campaign, ad set/ad group and ad what the ROAS is.
whyImportant.description3: This means you can keep track of how effective that part of your online advertising campaign is at all different levels.
whyImportant.description4: A ROAS of 1 means you are spending exactly the same amount of money as you are earning of a conversion. If you spend $10 to sell a $10 product, the platform will indicate a ROAS of 1.
whyImportant.description5: Simply put, this means you break even. However, you must also take other costs into account like cost of goods, shipping costs, transaction costs, VAT, and maybe other costs. This is where the Break Even ROAS comes in.
whyImportant.description4_product: A ROAS of 1 means you are spending exactly the same amount of money as you are earning of a conversion. If you spend $10 to sell a $10 product, the platform will indicate a ROAS of 1.
whyImportant.description4_service: A ROAS of 1 means you are spending exactly the same amount of money as you are earning from a conversion. If you spend $10 to win a $10 job or sale, the platform will indicate a ROAS of 1.
whyImportant.description5_product: Simply put, this means you break even. However, you must also take other costs into account like cost of goods, shipping costs, transaction costs, VAT, and maybe other costs. This is where the Break Even ROAS comes in.
whyImportant.description5_service: Simply put, this means you break even. However, you must also take other costs into account like direct delivery cost, travel, platform fees, VAT, and maybe other costs. This is where the Break Even ROAS comes in.

formula.title: The Break Even ROAS Formula
formula.description: First of all, you have to add up all your costs together. Then by using the formula below you can calculate the ROAS at which a campaign, ad set/ad group or ad is profitable.
formula.exampleDescription: Suppose you sell a product for $30, cost of goods are $8 & the shipping costs are $2.
formula.exampleResult: This means that for every campaign, ad set/ad group or ad that has a ROAS higher than 1.5, you make a profit.
formula.exampleDescription_product: Suppose you sell a product for $30, cost of goods are $8 & the shipping costs are $2.
formula.exampleDescription_service: Suppose you price a job at $30, direct delivery costs are $8 & travel or materials are $2.
